items.title: Moonfire Faire seasonal event returns to Final Fantasy XIV on August 12, 2026
Final Fantasy XIV "Moonfire Faire" event kicks off Aug. 12th, 2026
items.content:
0 lightbox#closeBackground keyup@window->lightbox#closeWithKeyboard" class="hidden animated fadeIn fixed inset-0 overflow-y-auto items-center justify-center z-9999"> Final Fantasy XIV is finally available on Switch 2, and that means we can finally talk all about the exciting content and events lined up for the game, and that includes the Moonfire Faire!

The Moonfire Faire event runs from August 12, 2026 at 4:00 a.m. to August 26, 2026 at 10:59 a.m. (EDT). To get started, you need to be at level 30 and meet with Mayaru Moyaru the Lalafell at Limsa Lominsa Upper Decks (X:11.5, Y:13.8). This will kick off the “Earning Your Water Wings” questline that eventually allows you to earn the Inflatable Mograft mount along with the Lawn Bomb Raft, Lawn Chocobo Raft, and Lawn Mograft furnishings. The wall-mounted Moonfire Faire MMXXV and Moonfire Faire MMXVII Advertisements and tabletop Moonfire Faire MMXXV Advertisement are also part of the rewards. You can get a closer look at all the goodies in the image below.

In the time of the Ancients, Etheirys was divided across ten and three reflections to avert a terrible calamity. Thus, for twelve thousand years did the star survive, and by its enduring hope did the Warrior of Light at last thwart its Final Days. Yet victory comes at a cost, and fate now demands its due.

Faced with the new threat of the Solstice, the Warrior of Light is summoned to the Fourth reflection. But what do they hope to gain from wandering a world lost to ice? Hold fast to your convictions and join with your comrades as you brave the ever-expanding world of FINAL FANTASY XIV!

items.title: Square Enix is aware of Final Fantasy XIV’s long load times on Switch 2, is working on a fix
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV launched on Switch 2 yesterday and by most accounts, it is a success. Bringing the absolutely massive game to Nintendo’s hybrid console,
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV launched on Switch 2 yesterday and by most accounts, it is a success. Bringing the absolutely massive game to Nintendo’s hybrid console, players now have a new way to kill time when they are on the go or really need to use the bathroom (why am I always thinking about the bathroom with MMOs?). There have been some issues, though, and one is a bit of a mood killer: long load times.

On its official website , Square Enix confirms it is aware of the elongated waits between areas and is looking into a fix for them. “Our investigation has confirmed that, when a player enters an instanced duty while surrounded by many characters, loading data will take longer than usual, which lasts until the player leaves the instance,” writes the publisher. It then lists a number of specific instances where delays are noticeable. These include:

The company writes that the main issue seems to be related to “data reloading and cache clearing,” which are being optimized in a forthcoming update. The update will be available as soon as possible, though that could mean anything really. Still, I imagine Square Enix wants Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2 to be a compelling product rather than a gimmick, so I would expect a patch in a week or so.

Peter has been a freelance gaming and film critic for over seven years. His passion for Nintendo is only matched by the size of his collection.

items.title: FINAL FANTASY XIV Online, Big Walk, Lies of P: Complete Edition, Parkasaurus, Kynseed, and Rod Land hit the Switch
items.content:
Categories New Nintendo Downloads 5 August 2026 by Matt Gander With Elden Ring, The Duskbloods, Lords of the Fallen II , and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty on the horizon, the Switch 2 is about to become a second home for Souls-likes. Kickstarting this trend is this week’s Lies of P: Complete Edition , which is going down well with critics, reportidly boasting smooth performance. Hopefully they aren’t telling fibs.

“By bundling the base game with the phenomenal Overture expansion, Lies of P: Complete Edition is the ideal way of playing this tremendous soulslike for the first time. There are some caveats, but performance on Switch 2 is largely solid, with multiple graphics settings available to choose from,” said Tech Radar .

The Switch 2 is about to get another older Final Fantasy, and it’s a big one – the almighty FINAL FANTASY XIV Online , complete with all the expansions. A few different versions are available, including a £11.99 starter edition, the £44.99 complete edition, and an £87.99 collector’s edition with a lengthy list of bonus items. If you’re curious, Square-Enix has released a 30 day free trial, which according to Eurogamer doesn’t require NSO.

On track to become one of the highest rated games of the year is Big Walk – aka what the Untitled Goose Game developers did next. The Metacritic for this online co-op jaunt – which true to its name, involves going on a big walk – currently sits at an impressive 93%. Communication plays a big part, with various ways to talk to friends, from whiteboards to walkie-talkies. Obstacles meanwhile can be overcome in various ways, lending a sandbox feel, and there’s plenty of potential for messing around.

Another game reviewing well is Kynseed , a life sim created by ex-Fable staff, and consequently rife with good ol’ British humour. “Kynseed is bountiful with tasks to do, NPCs to please, and lands to discover. Oftentimes that quantity seems to take priority over quality, though that doesn’t always detract from the pops of dopamine you get when you complete a microtask,” said Nintendo Life .

Atari are back too with Parkasaurus: Dinoluxe Edition – a colourful park builder, in which it’s possible to breed dinos, all while creating exhibits to maintain guest happiness. The Sea Monsters and Prehistoric Wonders DLCs are included.

Then there’s the creature capturing deck builder Montabi , mini-game package Grizzy and the Lemmings – Crazy Party , physics-based destruction game Limbot , roguelike adventure Talespinner , and the self-explanatory Spooky Spirit Shooting Gallery for Nintendo Switch 2.

If you purchased the Virtual Boy add-on, you’ll find two previous unreleased games to play : D-Hopper and Zero Racers . Both were cancelled following the VB’s poor sales, and so they’ve lingered in Nintendo’s vaults ever since. D-Hopper is a top-down action adventure that uses the VB’s illusion of depth to good effect, while Zero Racers is a F-Zero spin-off with flying vehicles and tunnels to traverse. Think along the lines of Red Alarm , only a racer not a shooter. Apparently, it has no music, which makes us wonder how complete it is.

Sunsoft’s Route16 – an arcade game from 1981 – is being dusted off for a new collection that includes the original, the 1985 sequel, and new entry ROUTE16R . They’re available singularly if you’d rather go down that…route. Another surprise re-release is the Famicom version of Rod Land – a much-loved single screen platformer. Features include a gallery, a rewind tool, the ability to record your best time, and “a little extra content after completing the main game.”

This week’s EGGCONSOLE release meanwhile is ELTHLEAD – a strategy game from 1988 – while the latest Arcade Archives release is Konami’s 1987 military training sim Combat School . ASCII’S UFO -A day in the life- from 1999 gains a Console Archives release too, in which you must rescue missing aliens while witnessing human interactions. Sadly, it remains untranslated. Combat School should be worth a look, though.

Big Walk is a cooperative multiplayer adventure about teamwork and talking.

Set out with your friends through a wide-open world full of challenges, puzzles, and discoveries. You’ll need to work together to find your way around, stay in contact using an assortment of tools and toys, and figure out new ways to communicate when you suddenly find yourself speechless.

Adventuring aside, there’s plenty of time to just hang out. Sit and watch the sunset, or steal your friend’s binoculars and kick them into the ocean. Spending time with friends is the best part of a big walk.

Begin your adventure in FINAL FANTASY XIV: A Realm Reborn

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV launches a free trial on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: The most popular MMORPG finally arrives to Nintendo SWitch 2, and you can try it for free.
items.content:
The gates to Eorzea have officially opened on Nintendo Switch 2, and this time, you don't need to buy a ticket. Square Enix has launched the Final Fantasy XIV Free Trial on the new console, giving curious adventurers the chance to experience one of the world's most successful MMORPGs without paying a subscription or worrying about a time limit.

Calling it a "trial" almost feels misleading. Rather than offering a brief taste of the game, the free version includes the entirety of A Realm Reborn and the first three expansions— Heavensward , Stormblood , and Shadowbringers . New players can journey through an enormous story spanning hundreds of quests, challenge iconic bosses, clear dungeons and raids, and experiment with every available combat, crafting, and gathering job up to level 80. It's enough content to keep most RPG fans occupied for months.

One of Final Fantasy XIV's biggest strengths is its flexibility. A single character can learn every class in the game, allowing players to swap between roles whenever they like instead of creating multiple characters. Whether you prefer charging into battle as a tank, keeping allies alive as a healer, dealing massive damage, or taking a break to become Eorzea's finest blacksmith or fisherman, the Free Trial lets you experience nearly every side of the game.

As generous as it is, the trial isn't completely unrestricted. Free accounts cannot use the Market Board, trade items with other players, create parties or Free Companies, send direct messages, or participate in PvP modes. There's also a cap of 300,000 gil, ensuring the trial remains focused on exploration and story rather than the game's player-driven economy.

There's one important detail for newcomers: the Free Trial is only available for new service accounts. Once an account purchases the full game, it permanently transitions to the standard version, which requires a monthly subscription after the included game time expires. For that reason, players may want to squeeze every last dungeon, raid, and side quest out of the trial before making the jump.

Switch 2 owners should also make sure they have plenty of room to spare. Final Fantasy XIV requires around 117 GB of free storage, making it one of the largest downloads currently available on Nintendo's latest console. On the bright side, there's no need for a Nintendo Switch Online membership to play, so once the game is installed, the only thing standing between you and your next adventure is deciding which job to level first.

For anyone who's been waiting for the right moment to see what all the excitement is about, this might be it. With four complete chapters of the saga available at no cost, the Switch 2 Free Trial offers an adventure that's less of a demo and more of a full-blown fantasy epic. items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Coins Used for FFXIV Switch 2 Subscriptions
items.summary: You can only buy Final Fantasy XIV Switch 2 subscriptions and some other items with the new FFXIV Coins currency.
items.content:
Square Enix went over the new Final Fantasy XIV Coins currency used for things like subscriptions that the Switch 2 version of FFXIV and its expansions through Dawntrail are available. These will be purchased from the eShop. However, as the subscription will be waved for about a month after launch as the company ensures the MMORPG is running properly, that currency will only be used for account services and Online Store optional items at the moment. No Nintendo Switch Online subscription is required to play, though there is a perk for people who have one and are going through the game.

Square Enix didn’t explain what the exchange rate will be for FFXIV Coins on the Switch 2 in its announcement. It only noted that will be the way people will need to pay for things tied to real money in the MMORPG. When someone buys them on the eShop, they will be credited to a Square Enix Account. Those could then be used on Mog Station or to get things like mounts, cosmetics, Home World Transfer Services, Character Renaming Services, Fantasia, or Tales of Adventure in the Online Store . It also noted that, in order to be sure the currency shows in your account, someone would need to close the MMORPG after buying them and log in again.

The Nintendo Switch Online Perk doesn’t require any additional in-game actions or purchases. The bonus lets someone get another free Aetheryte as a free destination. This means one more place someone could teleport to without paying gil.

As a reminder, multiple versions of FFXIV are available on the Switch 2 at launch and don’t initially require a subscriptions to play. The base game is $19.99. There is also a Complete Edition for $59.99 that includes all expansions and Dawntrail. The Complete Collector’s Edition is $139.99 and goes up through Dawntrail and has all of the original collector’s edition items from the main MMORPG and expansions.

Final Fantasy XIV is available for the PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC, the Switch 2 version arrives on August 4, 2026, and the new expansion FFXIV Evercold debuts in January 2027.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Out Now on Switch 2, Complete Edition 30% Off Until August 8
items.summary: Square Enix has officially launched Final Fantasy XIV for the Nintendo Switch 2 today. To celebrate the release of [...]
items.content:
Square Enix has officially launched Final Fantasy XIV for the Nintendo Switch 2 today.

To celebrate the release of the game, the Complete Edition is currently available for $41.99, which is a 30 percent discount on the Nintendo eShop until August 8. After this the price will increase to $59.99.

The Switch 2 version will not require a Nintendo Switch Online subscription, however, a separate monthly subscription from the other versions will be required. Users who subscribe on other platforms will receive a 50 percent discount on the subscription for the Switch 2 version.

The Free Trial version of the game lets gamers play through the base game and the first three story expansions Heavensward , Stormblood , and Shadowbringers for free. The rest of the content requires a subscription

The Evercold expansion will launch in January 2027 for all platforms.
